gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watts each 2 kWh station burns just keeping its AC inverter on with nothing plugged in: The Solar Lab reports about 27 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, 17 W for the DJI Power 2000, about 18 W for the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, 9.5 W for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 and about 6 W for the Anker SOLIX S2000.
standout_why: Compared against popsci.com Black Friday deals (cited), us.ecoflow.com Black Friday page (cited), outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000 (cited), outagereadyhq.com, thewattlist.com and powerreserveguide.com. None gives an idle or no-load watt figure for any unit. The closest is outagereadyhq's flat 'count 85% of the battery as usable, because the inverter uses some energy itself', the same flat 85% ChatGPT used. Rivals do print X-Boost and lifting watts (outagereadyhq, powerreserveguide, thewattlist), and thewattlist says the AC180's lifting mode is 'for resistive heat loads', so the lifting-mode point is only partly new. Two cited pages, businessinsider.com and popularmechanics.com, could not be opened (fetch blocked), so they are unchecked; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: The page's ranking (capacity and continuous watts per dollar) is unchanged; idle draw is the tie-breaker for the use ChatGPT assumed (fridge, Wi-Fi, lights through an outage, AC left on all day). At 24 h with AC on, idle alone takes about 648 Wh (32% of 2,048 Wh) on the DELTA 3 Max, 408 Wh (20%) on the DJI Power 2000, 432 Wh (21%) on the C2000 Gen 2, 228 Wh (11% of 2,073.6 Wh) on the Elite 200 V2 and 144 Wh (7% of 2,010 Wh) on the S2000. That backs the Elite 200 V2 over the DELTA 3 Max, which was ChatGPT's first-chat pick at near the same price, and narrows the DJI Power 2000's lead for low-load backup. The S2000 has the lowest idle but only 1,500 W output and a long ship time. Second point: BLUETTI's 3,900 W Power Lifting figure is, in BLUETTI's own words, for 'pure resistive loads', so the Elite 200 V2's ceiling for motors and compressors is its 2,600 W rating.

findings.label: Why a station drains with nothing plugged in
findings.value: "the inverter itself requires energy to stay on and to ensure the power inside the unit's batteries is ready for action"; the display, fans, control electronics and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth add to it
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: idle consumption how-to
findings.note: The Solar Lab's own definition: 'idle consumption refers to the energy a power station uses just to stay on'. The page gives no formal test method; its one example is an estimate of over 70 W for the Anker F3800.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC inverter on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Review: A Step Forward or a Step Sideways?
findings.note: 'After a few tests, we calculated the idle consumption at about 27 watts' with the AC inverter left on; the review estimates about three days of standby. Arithmetic: 2,048 Wh / 27 W = 76 h; 27 W x 24 h = 648 Wh/day, 32% of rated capacity. Same review: efficiency 79% (load not stated), weight 45 lb. No author or date shown.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC inverter on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: DJI Power 2000 review
findings.note: 'With the AC inverter left on, it consumed right around 17W idling', which the review says 'translates to about 5 days of idle runtime'. Arithmetic: 17 W x 24 h = 408 Wh/day, 20% of 2,048 Wh. Same review: efficiency about 84% (load not stated), 48.5 lb.

findings.label: Maker spec page: AC output and standby figure
findings.value: DYM2000L: AC 100-120 V, 25 A, 50/60 Hz; 2,048 Wh; approx. 22 kg; over 80% capacity after 4,000 cycles; no standby or idle power listed
findings.note: The spec page gives volts and amps, not a watt rating: 120 V x 25 A = 3,000 VA by arithmetic. It lists no peak watts, no UPS switchover time and no AC recharge time.

findings.label: Idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback?
findings.note: 'coming in at just 9.5W per hour'; the review does not say whether the AC inverter was on or how it was measured. The Solar Lab says it bought the unit itself. Same review: efficiency 94% (load not stated), 53.4 lb. Arithmetic: 9.5 W x 24 h = 228 Wh/day, 11% of 2,073.6 Wh; 2,073.6 / 9.5 = 218 h.

findings.label: Idle draw as listed in The Gadgeteer's feature list
findings.value: 10 W with AC and DC left on; UPS 15 ms; 24.2 kg / 53.4 lb
findings.source_title: The Gadgeteer: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 portable power station review (Greg Cleveland)
findings.note: 'Low idle consumption, 10w/h with AC and DC left on' sits in the bulleted 'Other features' list, so it reads as a maker-supplied claim, not Cleveland's measurement. He calls the advertised 15 ms 'on the edge of being too long' for switchover but found no issues in use. Published 2025-01-06, updated 2026-11-02.

findings.label: Power Lifting, in BLUETTI's words
findings.value: "effortlessly supports pure resistive loads of up to 3,900W" (examples given: kettles, electric blankets, hair dryers)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station (BLUETTI US store)
findings.note: The 3,900 W figure applies to resistive heating loads only; a fridge compressor or pump is limited by the 2,600 W continuous rating. Same page: $899.00, 'expected to ship in early January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18', AC input 1,800 W, 80% in 1.1 h, full in 1.4 h, 5-year warranty. The page gives no idle figure, UPS time or weight.

findings.label: Idle draw: Anker's claim
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US)
findings.note: 'With just 9W of idle power consumption, it can power a portable fridge for 7 days or a dual-door fridge for up to 32 hours.' No test conditions are given for the 9 W. Same page: 2,400 W rated, 4,000 W peak, UPS 10 ms, 41.7 lb, and 'all C2000 Gen 2 orders placed on or after November 26th will ship within 6–12 weeks'. The page text showed no price.

findings.label: Idle draw with AC outlets on standby (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 review
findings.note: 'In our real-world testing with AC outlets on standby mode' idle 'sat closer to 18W per hour'; it says Anker's 9 W 'is true if you only have the screen and USB ports active'. Arithmetic: 18 W x 24 h = 432 Wh/day, 21% of 2,048 Wh. Same review: efficiency about 89%, 42 lb.

findings.label: Idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Anker SOLIX S2000 review
findings.note: 'the unit consumed only about 6 watts per hour'. Arithmetic: 6 W x 24 h = 144 Wh/day, 7% of 2,010 Wh. Same review: efficiency 91%, about 36 lb, 1,500 W inverter.

findings.label: X-Boost on EcoFlow's Black Friday page (cited by ChatGPT)
findings.value: page lists 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, member price $879 and non-member $1,199; no X-Boost, surge or idle figure for this model
findings.note: ChatGPT's first chat quoted an $854 member price and $899 regular; the page read today shows $879 member and $1,199 non-member. The Solar Lab's DELTA 3 Max review says X-Boost 'always seemed like a gimmick to us from the start'.

unsourced: BLUETTI's manual wording on how Power Lifting works (the lowered output voltage) and the ECO mode auto-shut-off thresholds and hours: the manual PDF downloaded from s4.bluettipower.com but could not be converted to text, so nothing from it is used.
